summary: Discourse representation structures with atomic, identity, negation, implication and disjunction conditions, interpreted in the models of DPL.v by verifying embeddings, and their translation into dynamic predicate logic: a box becomes existential quantification over its universe followed by the conjunction of its conditions. The translation is correct in both directions up to pointwise equality of assignments, truth is preserved, and the donkey DRSs get the truth conditions of DPL.v. A counterexample shows that reading DPL conjunction as DRS merge fails when a variable is reused.

sources.citation: Kamp, H., van Genabith, J. & Reyle, U. (2011). Discourse Representation Theory. Handbook of Philosophical Logic, vol. 15. Springer.
Muskens, R. (1996). Combining Montague semantics and discourse representation. Linguistics and Philosophy 19(2):143-186.
Groenendijk, J. & Stokhof, M. (1991). Dynamic Predicate Logic. Linguistics and Philosophy 14(1):39-100.

evidence: DRAFT for the author's review; not an accepted source-level verdict.
DRT and DPL are interpreted in the same models, those of DPL.v, which the file leaves unchanged.
The file's header says that section, definition and page numbers for its three sources are still to be added.
Accessibility as a syntactic relation, a translation from DPL to DRT, and duplex conditions are listed in the file as not formalized.

determination_rationale: DRAFT for the author. The sources' definitions are rendered relationally. One result, drt_dpl_meaning, uses function extensionality; the others print as closed.

artifact_classes.description: the exact equality of the two relations needs function extensionality, because DPL tests return the input assignment itself
a universe is a list of variables; 'differs at most on the universe' is stated pointwise
